overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by untimely approving minutes for two meetings and by failing to complete members' certification forms. No remedial order issued because the Committee has disbanded.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to timely approve minutes for meetings held March 30 through May 26; the AG found two meetings' minutes were not timely approved.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law where it failed to timely approve minutes for meetings held on April 7 and May 11.

allegations.summary: Of the other minutes challenged as untimely, the AG found they were approved within the later of three meetings or 30 days.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the remainder of the meeting minutes at issue here were approved within the later of three meetings or 30 days and therefore were timely approved.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged some Committee members never signed Open Meeting Law certification forms; the Committee did not provide the forms to the AG despite requests.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the certification forms were not properly completed, and that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law as alleged.

allegations.summary: AG found the Committee did not meet within 14 business days of receiving the complaint to review it and respond in writing to the complainant, with copy to the AG.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not comply with these requirements.

allegations.summary: Complaint included allegations that the Committee did not timely or fully respond to public records requests for minutes and documents.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review those allegations as they fall under the purview of the Supervisor of Records within the Secretary of the Commonwealth’s office.
